summary: A cheap, well-isolated probe of SGLang's single-token align under EP, but its stated cost model is wrong: on master the bs=1 align is already SGLang's one-launch small-batch kernel over 32 experts (below 4.9 us, not in the bs=1 top-4), so the realistic upside is ~2-4 us of 80 us on decode_1 only (<1% overall, inside the +/-1.5% CI). Single result is interpretable from the per-shape bs=1 number and its top-kernel list; no companion needed.
justification: Mechanism: for one token the 8 ids are distinct, so a single-token align needs no histogram/cumsum and can write 8 blocks (one per id) directly; that is plausibly a smaller kernel than moe_align_block_size's small-batch kernel. But the hypothesis overstates what it replaces. (1) FINDINGS/BEST.json top_kernels for bs=1 on master are Marlin 41.1 us, at::reduce_kernel 5.6, unrolled_elementwise 5.4, elementwise 4.9 -- the align kernel is not in the top four, so it costs <4.9 us; at bs=32 the same kernel (moe_align_block_size_small_batch_expert_kernel) is 6.7 us. (2) The landed parity patch already shrank the align to 32 experts and (per its own md) dropped sorted_ids under the 4096 fused-padding threshold, so 'a 256-expert histogram, 2-3 launches' does not describe master; it is one small-batch launch over 32 counters plus possibly a zeros() for the cumsum buffer. (3) Under EP the single-token kernel will, if it tolerates -1 at all, most likely emit 8 blocks with block_experts = -1 for the 6-7 remote slots (n_padded = 8*block_size_m = 64 rows at block 8) where the general align emits only the 1-2 local blocks; Marlin with is_ep=True skips expert -1 blocks, but it now iterates 8 m-blocks instead of 1-2, so a few hundred ns could come back on the Marlin side. Expected shapes/directions are consistent with TASK.md (only bs=1 changes code; bs=8/16 are true controls since num_tokens==1 is the branch), and the bs=1 pre-timing test exercises exactly this path so correctness is covered. Magnitude: 2-4 us on a 60-weight shape at 80.2 us is 2.5-5% on decode_1, roughly 0.4-0.8% on the geomean -- detectable per shape (bs=1 err_ns is 479 ns, ~0.6%) but invisible in the overall CI, so this run is a per-shape learning, not a submit candidate. Weakest link: the gain budget is the align kernel's own few microseconds, and master already runs its cheapest variant; the hypothesis has not measured what it is removing. Also note master is 3.2 us SLOWER than SGLang at bs=1 (80.2 vs 77.0, outside the 0.48 us error) even with the 32-expert align, so even a full success here only restores parity on decode_1 and the unexplained 16 us of generic at::native kernels (reduce_kernel, unrolled/elementwise) at bs=1 is the bigger target.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity (the only landed item) changed moe_align_block_size's num_experts from 256 to 32, which is the exact kernel this hypothesis replaces at bs=1: the measured delta is 'single-token align vs 32-expert small-batch align', smaller than the 'vs 256-expert align' the hypothesis text argues from. This does not confound attribution (the 32-expert align is master and the right comparator); it only shrinks the expected gain. A flat result means the single-token kernel is not cheaper than the 32-expert small-batch kernel, which is the question that matters for master.

sglang-marlin-path-parity also fixed is_ep=True, block_size_m=8 at bs=1 and the fused sorted_ids padding; under the single-token path n_padded becomes 8*block_size_m regardless of how many local experts the token hits, so any loss could sit in Marlin's m-block loop (8 blocks, 6-7 skipped as -1) rather than in the align itself. The result's per-kernel list for bs=1 separates these without another run: Marlin time up => block-count cost; align kernel time down => the align won.
interference: No companion warranted. The change is a single kernel swap on one shape with two in-file controls (bs=8, bs=16 keep the general align), and both outcomes are interpretable: a gain on decode_1 is attributable to the swap (nothing else differs from master), and a loss is attributable to the swap plus the Marlin 8-block side effect, which the profile's per-kernel times resolve. An ab-revert of the parity align count (256 experts) would answer 'does single-token beat the 256-expert align', which no longer matters since 32 is master. In-flight marlin-block-size-m-next-larger (block 16 at bs=1) does not change the picture (n_padded 128 vs 64, still 8 blocks); in-flight triton-w13-grouped-gemv-small-m and queued triton-w2-grouped-gemv-small-m would supersede this at bs<=8 if they land (the align leaves the small-M path entirely once w2 moves), which the hypothesis already states -- so merge ordering, not a companion, decides whether this stays relevant. A control isolating 'align cost' from 'Marlin 8-block cost' would need a compaction kernel that is itself a new change; not worth a run.
rules_flags: None that break a rule. The num_tokens==1 branch is shape-only; moe_align_single_token returns device tensors (n_padded stays on device) so no host sync; nothing derived from data is cached; precision path (W4A16 Marlin, FP32 reduce, BF16 activations) is untouched.

Minor: the lazy `from ... import moe_align_single_token` inside kernel_fn (copied from baseline) is host-only Python and harmless under graph replay, but hoist it to module level so an ImportError surfaces at import time rather than inside the bs=1 test.
open_questions: Does moe_align_single_token exist in the judge's SGLang build and accept ids containing -1? Nothing in this problem has ever executed that import (baseline reaches it only when expert_map is None, never under ep8). An ImportError or a -1 index fault fails the bs=1 pre-timing test and should be logged as do-not-retry.

What does the single-token kernel emit for a -1 id: a block with block_experts=-1 (Marlin is_ep skips it), or does it drop the slot and compact (n_padded = local_count*block_size_m)? The former costs Marlin 6-7 skipped blocks; the latter is the ideal. Read SGLang's source before building if available.

What is the align kernel's actual time at bs=1 on master? It is absent from the top-4 (<4.9 us); the hypothesis's '2-3 launches over a 256-expert histogram' describes neither master (32 experts, fused padding) nor the small-batch kernel variant that profiles show. Get the number from the full profile txt of fb2cc736613747df if it is saved.

Why is master 3.2 us slower than SGLang at bs=1 (80.2 vs 77.0 us, err 0.48 us) despite the 32-expert align that was expected to make bs=1 faster? If the 32-expert small-batch kernel is for some reason slower than the 256-expert one at bs=1 (e.g. different branch of the wrapper), this hypothesis is testing on a shape whose align regression is unexplained.

The ~16 us of at::native reduce_kernel / unrolled_elementwise / elementwise kernels at bs=1 (20% of the shape) are a larger target than the align; what are they (the .to(int32)/.to(float32) copies, the expert_map gather, the Marlin wrapper's workspace zeroing, torch.zeros for the align cumsum)?
